scene.note: The ride board stops being typed in by hand and shows whatever Wilf writes in today.js.

steps.note: Wilf writes the date and the tram that runs today.
The board reads those values from the file instead of having them typed in.
Visitors see today's date and today's tram.
The plan has the first ride, the last ride and how many rides run an hour.
The board shows both times and works out how far apart the rides are.
On a busy day with more rides, the board says so by itself.
The plan has the adult fare, in pence.
The board turns each fare into money text, the child fare being half.
Families read both fares on the board.
Each tram in the plan has a photo and a name.
The board hands those values to its image.
The picture on the board is the tram that is really out today.
Each tram has its own colour, its livery.
The board paints its strip with that colour.
The strip matches the tram waiting at the stop.
